extracted.intended_audience: PR agencies, in-house communications teams and PR professionals considering or analysing PR Week Awards entries
extracted.subtask_description: Extract the explicit and implicit judging dimensions embodied in the PRWeek Awards 2024 results page — i.e., the award category headings and the qualities/evidence called out in each winning entry that signal what judges value.

rubrics_metrics.name: B2B CAMPAIGN
rubrics_metrics.description: Riverford’s Get Fair About Farming campaign stood up for oft forgotten farmers, lobbying for tangible change in the face of an issue which not only threatens the fabric of British farming, but directly affects every consumer that has ever shopped at a supermarket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals valued elements: defending/advocacy for stakeholders, lobbying for tangible policy/industry change, linking B2B action to consumer impact, clear target (supermarkets), social relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST ENVIRONMENTAL PURPOSE CAMPAIGN
rubrics_metrics.description: The ‘Where’s The Food?’ campaign aimed to secure government funding for surplus food redistribution, building on FareShare’s 2018/2019 pilot success. The campaign sought to highlight the program's social, economic, and environmental benefits, emphasizing its role in combating food waste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on: policy change/securement of funding, building on evidence/past pilots, multi-dimensional benefits (social/economic/environmental), clear calls to government, systemic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST INTEGRATED CAMPAIGN
rubrics_metrics.description: An insight (from a conversation) led to an international, news agenda‑leading PR campaign about mental health that drove nearly 2,000 pieces of coverage across five continents and saw its creative come to life in multiple executions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values: insight-driven idea, integration across channels, scale (international reach), earned media volume, creative executions translated across markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST INTERNATIONAL CAMPAIGN
rubrics_metrics.description: To launch new ice creams, the campaign brought together a major TikTok star and NASA sun sounds to create a summer anthem — a creative, culturally resonant idea deployed for product launch internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on cross-border creative localisation, celebrity/platform partnerships, cultural relevance, originality in media/creative approach, product launch impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST PR EVENT
rubrics_metrics.description: A cross‑generational collaboration between Camden Town Brewery and OG condiment brand HP that smashed social barriers and sales records through a targeted, fully integrated event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: audience targeting, creativity of concept, social/cultural impact, sales uplift, integration with brand and media amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST SOCIAL PURPOSE (ESG) CAMPAIGN
rubrics_metrics.description: Blurred’s 'I Am Not A Typo' project sought to correct inequalities of autocorrect, addressing disparity in how names are 'typoed' and reflecting multicultural UK realities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses social purpose clarity, relevance to underrepresented groups, originality, coalition-building (partners), measurable social impact or awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST USE OF A CELEBRITY(IES)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specsavers re-recorded a famously misheard song to start a public health conversation about hearing loss — using celebrity/creative music to make a hearing test impossible to ignore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on creative integration of celebrity, relevance to campaign objective (behaviour change/health), memorability, and public engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST USE OF CONTENT
rubrics_metrics.description: Specsavers turned a misheard song into a hearing test and content vehicle; other shortlisted work used narrative reimagining (e.g., Winnie‑the‑Pooh alternate tale) to frame environmental issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for content that tells a compelling story, reframes issues creatively, drives audience engagement and supports measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST USE OF CREATIVITY
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries such as Specsavers’ Misheard Version used creative reinterpretation of culture to start public health conversations; other winners reframed brand positioning via unexpected collaborations (e.g., Guinness in fashion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates originality, idea-to-execution creativity, cultural resonance, and demonstrable results from creative risk-taking.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST USE OF AN INFLUENCER(S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns partnering with TikTok creators to review public toilets and travel the country to create authentic, entertaining content that drove awareness for a consumer product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values authentic creator alignment, platform-appropriate execution, entertainment value, reach/engagement and fit with the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST USE OF PLANNING, STRATEGY AND EVALUATION
rubrics_metrics.description: Movember’s campaign to raise awareness of men’s mental wellbeing on World Suicide Prevention Day used targeted education on early signs and drove traffic to resources as part of an integrated measurement-focused programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses strategic insight, planning rigor, clearly defined objectives, measurement/evaluation frameworks, and evidence of impact (traffic, awareness, behaviour).

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST USE OF A SMALL BUDGET
rubrics_metrics.description: Testicular cancer awareness campaign used low-budget, high-impact creative to generate significant awareness and impact ahead of awareness month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges efficiency: creativity relative to budget, disproportionate impact, smart use of channels/resources, compelling idea that scales without big spend.

rubrics_metrics.name: CITY & CORPORATE COMMUNICATIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: Repositioning McAfee from enterprise seller to consumer-facing protector of individuals — carving an area of ownership and shifting public perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by clarity of repositioning, stakeholder mapping, reputation management, and effectiveness in shifting perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FINANCIAL SERVICES
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns that tell human stories behind financial products or drive national conversation about product tools (e.g., 'Share The Load' chore calculator capturing public attention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for storytelling that humanises financial services, drives product adoption or awareness, and earns media or behavioural outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: HEALTHCARE: ETHICAL & OTC CONSUMER
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that reframes public health conversations and encourages health-seeking behaviour (e.g., hearing tests) through non-scary, accessible creative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises ethical handling, regulatory compliance, clear public-health outcomes, and sensitive messaging that drives behaviour change.

rubrics_metrics.name: INTERNAL COMMUNICATIONS AND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns focused on employee safety, wellbeing and behaviour change within large organisations (e.g., behaviour-change safety campaigns; company-wide mental health initiatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed on relevance to workforce, measurable behaviour change, multi-channel internal tactics, leadership alignment and measurable engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISSUES AND REPUTATION MANAGEMENT
rubrics_metrics.description: Low-cost, high-impact campaign (e.g., Heathrow’s ‘The Fly Up’ biofuel breakfast) that changed narrative from flight-shaming to flight-applauding by communicating a clear plan of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values narrative reframing, crisis/issue navigation, credibility of solutions offered, cost-effectiveness and measurable change in public narrative or sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS: AUTOMOTIVE AND TRANSPORT
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns that use unexpected channels (e.g., transit stations/music) to recapture attention and drive donations or awareness for transport-related causes or brands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for channel innovation, relevance to traveller audiences, reach and conversion metrics, and creative use of environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS: CULTURE, MEDIA, SPORT AND TRAVEL
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that leverages cultural institutions or sports to broaden audience reach and deepen engagement (e.g., V&A advisory programme reaching core audiences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses cultural fit, audience development, reach, and how PR supports institutional goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS: LEISURE AND HOSPITALITY
rubrics_metrics.description: Insight-led PR programmes that reposition hospitality brands and tackle stigma (e.g., McDonald's mental health campaign driven by a single insight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by insight-to-idea pipeline, guest/customer engagement, integrated activations, and press/social impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS: HEALTH, BEAUTY, RETAIL AND FASHION
rubrics_metrics.description: Repositioning retailers as service providers (e.g., health & wellness partner) or taking brands into new cultural spaces (e.g., Guinness into fashion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated on brand repositioning, audience relevance, creative collaborations, and measurable business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOT-FOR-PROFIT
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose-driven campaigns (including non-client-initiated work) that correct inequalities, build public awareness and achieve measurable results for causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values authenticity, impact for beneficiaries, ability to mobilise partners/audiences, and measurable shifts in awareness or policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: PUBLIC AFFAIRS
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns seeking to influence regulation or government decisions (e.g., responses to changes in investor income thresholds affecting female founders), highlighting disproportionate impacts and mobilising stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on evidence-based arguments, coalition-building, political strategy, measurable policy outcomes or commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: PUBLIC SECTOR
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex behavioural-change public policy communications (e.g., Wales’ shift to 20mph default), focusing on increasing awareness and acceptance of legislative change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses handling of complexity, reach across communities, behaviour-change methods, and public acceptance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: TECHNOLOGY
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns tackling tech-related social issues (e.g., algorithmic misogyny), where invisible forces are made visible and public debate is advanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values clear articulation of complex tech problems, evidence, public education, platform/algorithm engagement, and stakeholder mobilisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST AGENCY OUTSIDE LONDON (HEADQUARTERS OUTSIDE M25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognises outstanding agency performance outside London: growth, client roster strength, team development and operational embedding of capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated on business growth, client portfolio quality, talent development and delivery against regional market needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: DIVERSITY, EQUITY & INCLUSION CHAMPIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisations that transparently report on DEI journeys, strive for continuous improvement and openly share successes and failures to drive industry change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on transparency, continuous improvement, concrete actions and measurable progress on diversity and inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEW CONSULTANCY OF THE YEAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Young consultancies that have launched recently and achieved substantial commercial success and growth relative to their short operating history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses rapid growth, commercial traction, client wins and successful scaling from small initial investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: YOUNG PR PROFESSIONAL
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual early in their career delivering exceptional results, building partnerships, securing national coverage, advising senior leadership and driving process improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates individual impact, leadership potential, results delivered, and breadth of responsibility beyond years of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPECIALIST CONSULTANCY OF THE YEAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultancies specialising in a niche (e.g., multicultural marketing) that deliver measurable societal impact and secure planning-table influence across clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on subject-matter expertise, societal outcomes, client influence and consistent delivery in a specialist area.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOUTIQUE CONSULTANCY OF THE YEAR (<£3M TURNOVER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller consultancies that deliver responsible growth, impactful work and nurture their people while achieving year-on-year success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values sustainable growth, people-focused culture, and clear evidence of impactful client work relative to size.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMALL CONSULTANCY OF THE YEAR (£3M-£10M TURNOVER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fast-growing small agencies delivering best-in-class PR with measurable effectiveness and new business wins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses growth rate, campaign quality, business development and contribution to client outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: MID-SIZED CONSULTANCY OF THE YEAR (£10M-£20M TURNOVER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mid-sized agencies demonstrating financial growth, creativity and industry recognition while sustaining culture and client service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on revenue growth, creative leadership, client retention and industry standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: LARGE CONSULTANCY OF THE YEAR (>£20M TURNOVER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large agencies investing in people and delivering work that pushes the industry forward while maintaining inclusive workplaces and commercial scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values scale, innovation at enterprise level, people investment and measurable impact on industry standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: IN-HOUSE TEAM OF THE YEAR (PRIVATE SECTOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small in-house teams that protect and promote corporate reputation across multiple businesses and markets, delivering measurable communications impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed on scope of responsibility, results for multiple business units, reputation protection and strategic communications outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: IN-HOUSE TEAM OF THE YEAR (PUBLIC/THIRD SECTOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public/third-sector communications teams that make complex or 'dry' subjects human and relevant to the public, cutting through noise to increase engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated on public engagement, simplifying complex policy/subjects, innovation and impact on public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEOPLE, AGENCIES & TEAMS — GENERAL (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Across people and agency awards the page highlights growth, creativity, people-centred culture, measurable results, and industry leadership as recurring success factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-criteria: commercial success (growth, turnover), creative recognition, people/culture metrics, client outcomes and awards/industry acclaim.
